text:
sana: Quick sync on the "spend-governor" idea for Dedicated pools. Need runnable plan + migration notes.
yves: Goal: let tenants set soft+hard spend limits per billing period. Autoscaler enforces by applying progressive mitigations.
kevin: mitigation chain proposal (in order): 1) switch to cheaper variant, 2) reduce max_tokens, 3) move to preemptible nodes, 4) throttle background jobs, 5) reject requests.
marta: important: autoscaler should emit the chosen mitigation and the reason. We need audit events for billing and legal.
raj: operator boundary: billing-service pushes aggregated spend delta to a small pub/sub topic. A "governor-adaptor" subscribes, validates, and writes readable BudgetStatus CRs (TTL). Autoscaler watches BudgetStatus, not billing-service.
yves: benefits: no coupling, CRs are reconciled, and k8s RBAC controls access. Also easier to replay for dry-run.
kevin: CRD sketch idea: budgetStatus: { tenant_id, period_start, cap_usd, consumed_usd, state } then pool config references pricing_tier + preferred_fallbacks.
sana: telemetry: need metric spend_governor_applied{tenant,action,src_pool} and trace span for decision with decision_id.
marta: rollout: 1) read-only mode where governor-adaptor writes BudgetStatus but autoscaler logs decisions without enforcing 2) enable mitigation 1-2 for pilot tenants 3) expand to mitigation 3 for non-SLA tenants 4) enable full enforcement.
raj: migration notes: legacy tenants with quota config should get auto-mapped to BudgetStatus with infinite cap unless set. Add a migration job that backfills consumed_usd for last 24h.
yves: question about fairness: if multiple tenants hit soft limits simultaneously, does the pool prefer higher-paying tenants? We need policy in DedicatedPool CR: priority_order: [sla_level, pay_rate, first_party].
kevin: tie-breaker: token-based fairness when pay_rate equal. Also implement soft reservations so critical tenants keep a min headroom.
marta: ops escape hatch: set cluster annotation spend-governor=disabled or patch governor-adaptor to stop updates. Document rollback runbook.
sana: can we support overflow to a tenant's hosted fallback? Add overflow_policy in BudgetStatus: allow_fallback_hosted, fallback_tier. Note privacy flag may be set to disallow.
raj: legal flag must be surfaced as budget_allow_fallback=false, governor-adaptor should honor it and emit event.
yves: implementation detail: governor-adaptor should sign CRs with digest of billing-report to ensure tamper evidence.
kevin: perf note: budget-adaptor write rate could be high. Use batching and only emit CRs when state changes or every 5m. Keep TTL of 10m.
marta: SLOs: autoscaler decision latency must be < 200ms from BudgetStatus watch to admission decision. Add unit tests around race when BudgetStatus expires mid-request.
sana: testing plan: unit tests, e2e with synthetic billing updates, canary in staging clusters across regions for 72h.
deploy-bot: Reminder: any change touching admissions requires deployment-guard true and 2-stage canary.
raj: follow-ups: Ill draft the CRD + adaptor proto; kevin will profile write paths; yves will write fairness heuristics doc.
yves: I'll also enumerate edge cases: duplicated billing messages, clock skew, read-after-write delays.
kevin: also think about cost accounting for model-switch mitigation: need per-variant token-cost model to estimate the cost delta before switching.
marta: schedule: RFC draft by EOD Fri, pilot list by next Wed. Thanks everyone. :pray:
